dossier.public_summary: The dip is very shallow (≈1.5%) and flat-bottomed but alternates between odd and even events about twice as deep as each other and varies strongly between sectors, with early sectors showing no transit and later ones showing deep dips. This odd-even pattern and sector-dependent depth are the signature of a blended eclipsing binary seen as a planet-like dip, not a small planet on the target.

reasons.why: Odd evens differ strongly (4.736 sigma, ratio 1.9, 48% difference) with same sign in all sectors and sector_oe_max_sigma 6.923, positively favouring an eclipsing binary at twice the period. Combined with extreme sector depth change and planet-like size/flat bottom this is best explained as a diluted binary (planet-like eclipse shape with odd/even depth change due to dilution/varying geometry), not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically within SPOC 2-min, from no detection (-16 ppm) to ~3100 ppm in later sectors, far beyond calibration. A real planet should be steady; this change indicates dilution/neighbour contamination or systematic blending, not a stable planet on the target.

reasons.why: Individual transits are inconsistent; two early transits are non-detections (5 and -39 ppm) and two late transits are much deeper (~3100 and 2856 ppm). High share from top 3 and p_consistent 2e-41 shows signal dominated by a few deep events, inconsistent with a planet transiting uniformly.
